title: Sequential derived realization retaining varying coefficient-ring actions
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and fix compatible universes and a small skeleton of its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B_n$ for $n\geq1$ and $R$ be sheaves of commutative rings on that site, with homomorphisms $q_{m,n}:B_m\to B_n$ for $m\geq n$ and $\pi_n:R\to B_n$ satisfying $q_{n,n}=1$, $q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m}$ and $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$. Write $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ for exact restriction of scalars along these maps, both on module sheaves and termwise on cochain complexes and their derived categories [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $M_n\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_n))$ and $\tau_{m,n}:M_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n$ satisfy $\tau_{n,n}=1$ and $\tau_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(\tau_{m,n})\tau_{r,m}$ under the canonical composition identifications. Set $\operatorname{Tow}_R(T)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, the category of strict inverse sequences with compatible levelwise maps [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

There exist integer-indexed cochain complexes $C_n$ of $B_n$-module sheaves, isomorphisms $i_n:[C_n]\xrightarrow{\sim}M_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_n))$, and $B_{n+1}$-linear chain maps $t_n:C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$ such that $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}(i_n)[t_n]=\tau_{n+1,n}i_{n+1}$. The composite chain map $t_{m,n}:C_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}C_n$ obtained from the adjacent maps satisfies $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(i_n)[t_{m,n}]=\tau_{m,n}i_m$ for every $m\geq n$. Any prescribed pair $(C_1,i_1)$ may be retained.

There is a cochain complex $S\in\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Tow}_R(T))$ whose degree-$d$ inverse sequence has terms $\operatorname{Res}_n C_n^d$, whose adjacent arrows are $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}(t_n)$ followed by scalar-restriction composition, and whose differential has components $d_{C_n}^d$. Its evaluations are these complexes, including all chain transitions, not merely their homology. In particular its localization $\mathcal M_\bullet=[S]\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_R(T))$ has derived evaluations canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Res}_nM_n$, carrying every evaluated transition to $\operatorname{Res}_m(\tau_{m,n})$. No boundedness, constructibility, or invertibility of transition-adjoints is assumed.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A_n=\operatorname{Mod}(B_n)$ and $\mathcal A_R=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. These categories are abelian by the small-site hypothesis. Restriction is the same underlying abelian sheaf with the action precomposed by the ring map; it is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. The exact-functor localization theorem therefore gives the stipulated termwise functors on unbounded derived categories and their natural cochain comparison isomorphisms. For $R\to B_m\to B_n$, the two restricted actions on a section $x$ are both $r\cdot x=\pi_n(r)x$, since $q_{m,n}\pi_m=\pi_n$. Similarly, successive $B$-restrictions have action $b\cdot x=q_{r,n}(b)x$. Thus the ordinary restriction compositors are identity on underlying sheaves and chain maps. Their canonical derived compositors respect the cochain comparisons by the exact-restriction composition lemma. In the subsequent equations suppress precisely these comparisons, not the coefficient actions.

source.place: Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), restriction functor preceding lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; exact localization as in derived.tex Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor).

proof.text: Write $Q_n$ for cochain localization into $D(\mathcal A_n)$. Choose a complex $C_1$ and an isomorphism $i_1:Q_1C_1\xrightarrow{\sim}M_1$; if the pair is prescribed, start with that very pair. Such representatives exist because the objects of the derived localization are complexes, up to the localization equivalence. The induction invariant at stage $n$ consists of the chosen pairs $(C_j,i_j)$ for $1\leq j\leq n$ and chain maps $t_j$ for $1\leq j<n$ satisfying $\operatorname{Res}_{j+1,j}(i_j)Q_{j+1}(t_j)=\tau_{j+1,j}i_{j+1}$. The invariant has no arrow condition at $n=1$.

source.place: Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category), objects of the localization; agent-written induction setup.

proof.text:
Suppose the invariant holds at $n$. Choose a complex $A$ of $B_{n+1}$-modules and an isomorphism $a:Q_{n+1}A\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{n+1}$. The arrow
$$g=\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}(i_n)^{-1}\tau_{n+1,n}a:Q_{n+1}A\longrightarrow Q_{n+1}(\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n)$$
is in $D(\mathcal A_{n+1})$. Quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A_{n+1})$ admit a right calculus of fractions, so the right-fraction representation lemma supplies an object $P$, a quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to A$ in the homotopy category and $f:P\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$ there with $g=Q(f)Q(s)^{-1}$. By definition of the homotopy category, choose actual chain maps representing $s$ and $f$; $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism since its homotopy class induces isomorphisms on cohomology. Set $C_{n+1}=P$, $t_n=f$, and $i_{n+1}=aQ(s)$. Then $i_{n+1}$ is invertible and
$$\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}(i_n)Q(t_n)=\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}(i_n)gQ(s)=\tau_{n+1,n}i_{n+1}.$$
The target $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}C_n$ and all previously chosen complexes and maps were fixed throughout. Recursion and choice over the positive integers yield all the desired pairs and adjacent maps. Every roof is taken inside the $B_{n+1}$-module category, so $t_n$ has the required $B_{n+1}$-linearity. In Lean, DerivedCategory.right_fac supplies the chain-level roof directly, so no separate quotient-map lifting is needed.

source.place: Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic), applied to K(Mod(B_{n+1})); categories.tex Tag 04VI (lemma-morphisms-right-localization), singleton case; agent-written recursive assembly.

proof.text:
Define $t_{n,n}=1$ and, for $m\geq n$, define
$$t_{m+1,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,m}(t_{m,n})t_m.$$
These are chain maps, with target identified by the restriction compositors of Step 1. Associativity of composition gives $t_{r,n}=\operatorname{Res}_{r,m}(t_{m,n})t_{r,m}$. Induct on $m-n$ to check the derived transition equation: the base is $1=\tau_{n,n}$, and the induction step, using Step 3 and the given cocycle, is
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,n}(i_n)Q(t_{m+1,n})
&=\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,m}(\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(i_n)Q(t_{m,n}))Q(t_m)\\
&=\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,m}(\tau_{m,n})\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,m}(i_m)Q(t_m)\\
&=\operatorname{Res}_{m+1,m}(\tau_{m,n})\tau_{m+1,m}i_{m+1}
=\tau_{m+1,n}i_{m+1}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the first equality includes exactly the cochain-compatible derived compositor of Step 1. In Lean, Nat.leRec defines these composites and its self/successor equations drive the identity, composition, and localization inductions.

source.place: Paragraph 2, implicit realization prerequisite: all composite coefficient transitions; agent-written calculation from the supplied cocycle.

proof.text: Restrict the constructed complexes to $R$ and write $E_n=\operatorname{Res}_n C_n$. Define $u_{m,n}:E_m\to E_n$ as $\operatorname{Res}_m(t_{m,n})$ followed by the identity-on-underlying-sheaves restriction compositor. On sections in every degree it is $R$-linear: $t_{m,n}(\pi_m(r)x)=q_{m,n}(\pi_m(r))t_{m,n}(x)=\pi_n(r)t_{m,n}(x)$. The identities and composition law for $t_{m,n}$ give $u_{n,n}=1$ and $u_{r,n}=u_{m,n}u_{r,m}$. Thus, for every degree $d$, the objects $E_n^d$ and arrows $u_{m,n}^d$ define an actual functor $S^d:\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal A_R$, hence an object of $\operatorname{Tow}_R(T)$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, implicit realization prerequisite: restrict the actual B_n-actions and chain maps to the common coefficient sheaf; agent-written construction.

proof.text: Define $d_S^d:S^d\to S^{d+1}$ by components $d_{E_n}^d$. The chain-map equation for $u_{m,n}$ is precisely $d_{E_n}^du_{m,n}^d=u_{m,n}^{d+1}d_{E_m}^d$, so these components are a natural transformation of inverse sequences. Its square is zero since $(d_{E_n})^2=0$ at every level, and morphisms of inverse sequences are equal when their components are equal. Therefore $(S^d,d_S^d)_{d\in\mathbf Z}$ is a cochain complex in $\operatorname{Tow}_R(T)$. Evaluation gives $E_n$ and $u_{m,n}$ as actual complexes and chain maps, by construction. In Lean this is the private transpose construction, whose asFunctor is definitionally the original diagram of complexes.

source.place: Paragraph 2, implicit realization prerequisite: interchange the complex and sequence indices; agent-written differential and naturality check.

proof.text:
The tower category is abelian and every evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_n$ is additive and exact by the levelwise-abelian theorem, applied to $\mathcal A_R$. Exact-functor derived factorization therefore gives
$$D(\operatorname{ev}_n)([S])\cong[\operatorname{ev}_n S]=[E_n]\cong\operatorname{Res}_n(Q_nC_n)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}_n(i_n)}\operatorname{Res}_nM_n.$$
These are the canonical evaluation comparisons for the chosen realization. The strict transition $\operatorname{ev}_m\to\operatorname{ev}_n$ on towers is a natural transformation; its termwise chain map on $S$ is exactly $u_{m,n}$. It descends through localization since naturality with an inverted quasi-isomorphism also gives naturality with its inverse. Consequently the evaluated transition under the displayed comparisons is $[u_{m,n}]$, followed by the restricted $i_n$. By Step 4 this equals $\operatorname{Res}_m(\tau_{m,n})$ preceded by the restricted $i_m$, with the restriction compositor on the target. This proves the transition clause in the derived category, not just after cohomology. The construction used neither boundedness nor any invertibility condition on the transitions.
